admission.justification: BUG-R59@v1 weighed marking masters Completed before cleanup against admitting PR-landed standalone masters inside _require_series_task_terminal, and the chosen cleanup-first order constrains future series finalization changes.

alternatives.option: Admit pull-request-landed standalone masters (sprint_ref is None, integration_strategy == 'pr', integration_status == 'completed', closeout_status != 'completed', empty pr_landed_standalone_blockers) inside _require_series_task_terminal's worktree_cleanup branch while keeping cleanup before task-document completion.
alternatives.reason: Preserves finalize's cleanup-before-task-documents order and promise ('Cleanup did not complete; task documents were not changed') for every series, also makes such masters directly cleanable by worktree_cleanup, and keeps worktree_abandon and sprint-commanded masters unchanged.

alternatives.option: Mark the master task document Completed before running cleanup inside lifecycle_finalize_task.
alternatives.reason: Would change the execution order for every series and could leave a master or commanding sprint row marked Completed when cleanup refuses.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Only if series cleanup and task-document completion are unified into a single atomic rollback-safe transaction or cleanup refusals can reliably roll back completed sprint rows.

consequences: Finalize keeps its universal cleanup-before-task-documents order and preserves 'Cleanup did not complete; task documents were not changed.' on cleanup refusal.
standalone_pr_landing.py owns the shared eligibility predicate and readiness blockers read by finalize.py, integration_branch_authority.py, and record_landing.py.
context: A pull-request-landed standalone master holds cleanup: pending and a non-Completed master document after worktree_record_landing, so lifecycle_finalize_task previously failed at cleanup because _require_series_task_terminal required status == 'Completed' before retiring the integration branch.
